newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks edge up after public holiday.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks edge up after public holiday.

text.p: Colombian stocks drifted up slightly in a session marked by deals in little-favored shares when trading reopened after Monday's public holiday, brokers said.

Bogota's IBB index ended 0.25 percent up at 870.46 on a volume of 1.56 million pesos, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed 0.07 percent up at 13,602.69 on a thin 599 million peso volume.
"Markets revolved around infrequently traded shares. The more popular shares were only traded in small volumes, but gave a certain stability to the market," a Bogota broker said.
"The Medellin exchange was dominated by cross deals between shareholders in the Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate," he added.
The highlight of the day's trading in Bogota was a 518.25 million peso deal in financial group Corporacion Financiera del Valle (Corfivalle) at a stable 7,350 pesos per share.

Building materials manufacturer Bison rose 33 percent above Friday's close to end at 683 pesos each on the back of a total volume of 390.1 million pesos. More than 190 million pesos in Banco de Bogota shares changed hands with the price edging up 0.01 percent to 6,011 pesos.

"The Bison deal was a tactic to push up the share price. These are classified as medium traded shares and lend themselves to those types of fluctuations. The rise did not have an impact on the general price index,"another Bogota broker said.

n Medellin, shares in chocolate manufacturer Compania Nacional de Chocolates remained unchanged at 8,400 pesos on a 186 million peso trade, while cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe fell 1.16 percent to 4,250 pesos on a 175 million peso volume.
